Performers
Francis Poulenc (piano four hands), Jacques Février (piano four hands) Documented

Both are named as pianists on the transferred Musidisc LP and on the earlier Club français du disque issue.

[3] [1] [4]
Work version
Original version for piano four hands Documented

All seven pieces are included. The two players’ primo and secondo assignments and their performing edition are not specified on the carrier.

[6] [3]
Recorded
1959-01-14 Documented

Diapason’s reissue credits give 14 January 1959 for this work and these pianists; the Archive item gives the recording year 1959.

[5] [1]
Place
Unknown Unknown

No recording venue is given in the consulted carrier, Archive or reissue credits.

Label
Musidisc, Collection Richesse Classique Documented[3]
Catalogue
RC 717 Documented

The transferred LP is dated 1970 by the Archive uploader. This is a later issue: the same work and pianists are catalogued by the BnF on Club français du disque 272, legal deposit 1962.

[3] [1]
Matrix, take, sides
band II: Manière de commencement through Piece II · band I: Piece III, En plus, Redite Documented

The transfer joins the work across the original LP side break. Matrix and take numbers are not supplied.

[3]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

The transfer engineer is not named. Internet Archive hosts the uploaded transfer.

Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The item’s 2025 upload date does not establish when the LP was transferred.

Processing
MP3 derivative of the uploaded FLAC transfer Documented

The file inventory identifies the FLAC parent. Playback equipment, equalisation, side-join procedure and restoration processing are not documented.

[2]
Composition rights
Public domain under the ordinary EU life-plus-70 term; Satie died in 1925. Inferred, not documented

The original score was published in 1911. This is a territorial assessment, not a worldwide permission statement.

[7] [6] [9]
Recording rights
EU public domain on the pre-1963 lawful-publication basis: the Poulenc–Février performance was issued on Club français du disque 272 by 1962. Inferred, not documented

The BnF legal-deposit record documents the 1962 issue; the 1959 session and performer/work identity connect it to the later Musidisc RC 717 transfer. Matrix-level take identity is not established. The 1970 reissue date is not used as the first-publication date. The former 50-year term expired before the 2013 extension. No Archive Creative Commons grant or US recording clearance is claimed.

[4] [1] [3] [5] [9] [10]

Erik Satie: Trois morceaux en forme de poire — Francis Poulenc and Jacques Février, piano four hands (1959). Club français du disque 272, published by 1962; transferred from Musidisc RC 717, hosted by Internet Archive. Territorial EU public-domain basis; US recording status not established. Rights statement

  1. Internet Archive: Poulenc and Février play Satie — Names both pianists, recording year 1959, Musidisc RC 717 and reissue year 1970.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  2. Internet Archive file inventory — Complete-work MP3 and its FLAC parent; FLAC duration 815.49 seconds; sleeve image attachments.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  3. Musidisc RC 717: transferred LP back sleeve — Performer names, catalogue, work and movement order, timings, and the split between sides A and B.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  4. BnF: Satie, 3 morceaux en forme de poire; Poulenc and Février — Club français du disque 272, one 45-rpm 17-cm disc, legal-deposit publication date 1962.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  5. Les Indispensables de Diapason: Erik Satie, Enregistrements 1937 à 1959 — Track 3 credits: Francis Poulenc, piano; Jacques Février, piano; recorded 14 January 1959. This later commercial remaster is a documentary source, not the streamed audio.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  6. Satie: Trois morceaux en forme de poire, R.L. & Cie. 9799 — Sibley Music Library scan of the Salabert reprint of the 1911 score; all seven movements, pp. 2–⁠31; composer dates 1866–⁠1925. Redite, pp. 30–⁠31: the upper part’s repeated figure precedes its bien chanté melody; the closing dynamics are piano in the upper part and pianissimo in the lower.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  7. BnF: Satie’s autograph, September 1903, RES-218 — Full title and the red-ink Recommendations on p. 30, signed 6 November 1903.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  8. Trois morceaux en forme de poire: composition and movement sources — Structure and music section identifies the reused cabaret songs, drawing on Steven Moore Whiting, Satie the Bohemian.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  9. Directive 2006/116/EC: term of copyright and related rights — Articles 1, 3 and 8: life-plus-70 authors’ term, former 50-year phonogram term, calendar-year calculation.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  10. Directive 2011/77/EU: extension of the phonogram term — Article 1(2)–(3): 70-year term and application to rights still protected on 1 November 2013.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
